channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Eco-Process Artist Residency 2026 · grunt gallery
item.description: One-month summer residency at Blue Cabin Floating Artist Residency in Metro Vancouver (August 2026) for emerging lens-based artists. Program focuses on eco-processing and alternative photographic techniques such as phytogram, lumen printing, cyanotype, and other sustainable photographic processes. Up to 3 mentorship sessions with interdisciplinary artist Morgan Sears-Williams. Blue Cabin is situated on the traditional territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations. Priority given to LGBTQ+ 2S emerging artists with some photo/lens-based experience. Open to emerging artists in Metro Vancouver and Indigenous territories/reserves connected to the region. Produced by grunt gallery in collaboration with Blue Cabin Cooperative. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,500 + materials + housing.

item.title: 2026 National Juried Photography Exhibition
item.description: Juried photography exhibition at the Academy Center of the Arts in Lynchburg, Virginia. Open to U.S. residents aged 18+. Photographs must be original work completed after January 1, 2021, not previously exhibited in a Lynchburg juried photography show. Juror Kiera Hight, photographer and filmmaker from Asheville, NC, selects work after installation. Exhibition runs September 4–25, 2026 with an opening reception on September 4. Digital submissions accepted via email or flash drive; JPEG, 300 DPI, minimum 4×6". — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,000 Best in Show.

item.title: Abbott Watts Photography Residency — Fall 2026 · Monson Arts
item.description: Dedicated photography residency at Monson Arts in Maine, with access to the photography studio and darkroom of Todd Watts in nearby Blanchard — adjacent to the former home of Berenice Abbott. Darkroom accommodates silver gelatin printing up to 40"×50" from 35mm to 8×10 negatives, plus alternative analog processes. Digital studio with PC workstations, 34" monitors, Adobe Creative Cloud, and a 44" Epson printer. Residents receive a private bedroom in shared housing in Monson, all meals, and a stipend ($250 for 2-week, $500 for 4-week). Fall 2026 sessions: September 14–24 (2-week) and October 28 – November 19 (4-week). Residents must supply their own materials and have a car (8-minute drive to studio). Open to photographers at any career stage worldwide. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Check site. Prize: Residency + stipend.

item.title: Peyton Evans Artist Residency (PEAR) 2026–2027 · The Studios of Key West
item.description: One-month residency program on Key West, Florida. Photographers apply under Media Arts. Residencies run the 2nd day of the month to the last day, between October 2026 and August 2027. Residents receive accommodation at the PEAR House (live/work space), a bike to get around the island, and access to shared kitchen facilities. No residency fee once accepted; artists cover their own travel, living expenses, and materials. Founded in 2006, The Studios has hosted hundreds of writers and artists; selection committees are comprised of working artists and professionals across Visual Arts, Literary Arts, Media Arts, Musical Arts, and Performing Arts. Apply via SlideRoom. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Check site. Prize: One-month live/work residency.

item.title: The City Series: Cambridge — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
item.description: Open call for The City Series: Cambridge, the inaugural edition of Shutter Hub's ongoing series of photobooks exploring the people, places, and cultures that shape cities worldwide. Photographers are invited to approach Cambridge openly — through people, atmosphere, details, routines, abstractions, or unexpected moments that feel personal — showing what the city feels like rather than what it looks like. Selected images featured in a printed publication available at shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Published in collaboration with Velvet Magazine. Pay-what-you-can entry with £10 minimum; free submissions available on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide. — Deadline: April 23, 2026. Fee: £10+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: The Colour Library: Yellow — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
item.description: Open call for The Colour Library: Yellow, part of Shutter Hub's curated series exploring the emotional, symbolic, and visual power of individual colours. This edition is dedicated to yellow — bold and joyful, energetic and optimistic, but also capable of signalling caution, unease, or something hauntingly strange. Welcomes all approaches from bold monochromes to subtle glows, conceptual or documentary. Selected photographers featured in a professionally produced photobook held in international collections including the British Library and V&A. 100 images will be selected. Featured photographers receive promotion and a dedicated page on the Shutter Hub website. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum. Free submissions on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide. — Deadline: July 16, 2026. Fee: £15+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: Lucie Foundation Scholarship Program 2026
item.description: Annual program offering four cash grants across two categories (Fine Art and Photojournalism/Documentary), each split between Professional and Emerging photographers. Prizes: Fine Art Professional $3,000 + Fine Art Emerging $1,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Professional $3,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Emerging $1,000 plus a Sony camera and lens. Winners featured in a group exhibition that travels to House of Lucie Galleries worldwide (Los Angeles, Athens, Budapest, Ostuni, Samui). 'Professional' means earning majority of income from photography; 'Emerging' means enrolled students, photographers in their first five years, or those who don't earn majority from photography. Early bird discounts: 20% off until April 23, 10% off until April 30. Applicants submit a project proposal (1,500 characters max), one-page bio/CV, and 20 digital images. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $15–25. Prize: $8,000.

item.title: PLACE/MEMORY — CONTACT Photography Festival · Northern Contemporary Gallery
item.description: Open call photography exhibition at Northern Contemporary Gallery in Toronto, presented as part of the 2026 CONTACT Photography Festival — Canada's largest photography festival. Photographers are invited to submit work that represents their current practice through the medium of photography, responding to the theme PLACE/MEMORY. Physical group exhibition runs May 21 – June 2, 2026, with an opening reception on May 21, 6–9pm. One submission per artist via the official Google form. Work drop-off May 19; pick-up June 3. Part of the CONSTELLATION program curated by Su-Ying Lee and Emilie Croning. — Deadline: May 12, 2026. Fee: Check site. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Art-in-Ed Workspace Residency 2026
item.description: 6–7 week workspace residency combining teaching with personal studio practice at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Artists teach intaglio, silkscreen, or hand papermaking to local public school students — fourth and/or eighth graders three days/week for three weeks in Spring (elementary) or high school students one day/week for 4 weeks in Fall (plus school visits). Outside of teaching, artists work independently in any WSW studio including darkroom photography. Residency includes $175/day per teaching day plus $525 for lesson planning, free housing, and 24/7 studio access. Artist covers travel and materials. Fall 2026 cohort teaches high school; Spring 2027 cohort teaches elementary. Applications open February 15; notification in July. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $175/day + $525 lesson planning.

item.title: Nordic Artists' Centre Dale 2027 Residency
item.description: Two-to-four-month residency in 2027 at NKD, a non-profit centre funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality in the village of Dale, Fjaler on Norway's west coast. Established 1998. Residents receive a monthly grant of NOK 11,000, up to NOK 5,000 in travel reimbursement, and free accommodation in a private residence house plus a 50m² studio with 6-metre ceilings and north-lit panorama windows. Open to professional visual artists, designers, and architects (photographers welcome). Not available to students or practitioners in music, writing, dance, or theatre. Residents give a presentation and participate in an open studio day. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: NOK 11,000/month.

item.title: Cavendish Arts Science Fellowship 2026–27
item.description: Annual fellowship in partnership with Girton College, Cambridge, supporting artists to engage with physicists and others at the Cavendish Laboratory. Runs October 2026 – October 2027 with a Cambridge residency of 6–12 months (can be split across visits). Includes £10,000 stipend, £10,000 production budget, up to £3,000 travel support, rent-free accommodation and meals at Girton College, and a studio/creative workspace plus flexible working spaces at the Cavendish Laboratory. Open internationally to artists of any medium or nationality — no prior science experience required. Must be 18+ and out of full-time education by October 2026. Joint applications accepted. — Deadline: May 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £23,000.

item.title: Chester Photo Festival 2026 — Making Voices Heard
item.description: Second edition of the annual Chester Photo Festival, running 16–29 October 2026 across University of Chester, Picturehouse, churches, and a museum. Theme: Making Voices Heard — exploring photography through myths, feelings, memories, and personal narratives. Free entry of up to 5 works; selection fees only apply if chosen (£45/work early deadline 15 May, £60/work late deadline 15 June, covering printing and standard framing). Open to photographers of all experience levels internationally. Accepts photography, moving image (online link + still), and artist books (PDF). Selected works included in the exhibition book and displayed across Chester venues. Late entries close when 300 works are selected. Organised by academics and researchers including Dr Alexandru Modoi and Professor Erik Knudsen. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: Free entry; £45–£60 per selected work. Prize: Exhibition + book publication.

item.title: BEERS London Group Exhibition 2026
item.description: Open call for a group exhibition of approximately 12 artists at BEERS London, a contemporary gallery in the heart of the City. All artistic media welcome including photography. Selected artists consigned for exhibition period plus up to three months, with 50/50 commission split on sales. Gallery actively promotes selected work to collectors. No guaranteed representation or sales. Open worldwide. Exhibition runs August–September 2026. Selected artists notified approximately four months before opening. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: £10. Prize: Group exhibition at BEERS London.

item.title: VISUAL Carlow 2027 Exhibition Open Call
item.description: Open call for exhibition proposals at VISUAL Centre for Contemporary Art in Carlow, Ireland, for a new commission in September 2027. Open to artists of all career stages working in any media, locally, in Ireland, or internationally — duos and groups welcome. Winning applicant receives a generous artist fee, significant production budget, and curatorial, production, technical, and marketing support. Shortlisted artists receive expansion fees to develop extended proposals. Four gallery spaces available (Main, Link, Studio, Digital). New commission only — existing work ineligible. Shortlist announced end of June 2026; expanded proposals due end of August 2026; winner announced September 2026. — Deadline: May 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Artist fee + production budget + exhibition.

item.title: L'OLTRE 2026 · The Docks
item.description: Open call from Naples-based photography association The Docks (founded 2020) inviting photographers and visual artists to explore visions that lie at the edges of conventional reality — beyond appearance, logic, and the visible. Winning project published as the first volume of L'OLTRE 2026 in a limited edition by The Docks Publishing. Honorable mentions featured on The Docks' channels as emerging artists. Fee is €15 total (€5 membership + €10 minimum donation). Open to all nationalities, genders, and ages. AI-generated works explicitly accepted. — Deadline: May 5, 2026. Fee: €15. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Joan Wakelin Bursary 2026
item.description: Annual £2,000 bursary for the production of a photographic essay on an overseas social documentary issue. Administered by the Royal Photographic Society in partnership with The Guardian. Winner also receives portfolio printing by Metro Imaging (up to 12 C-types at 16×12") and a portfolio review with Creative Director Prof Steve Macleod. Established in 2005 in memory of documentary photographer Joan Wakelin (d. 2003). Funds new original projects only; does not support ongoing projects or travel to/within war zones. Awarded to individuals, not groups. Open to all photographers worldwide. — Deadline: July 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £2,000 + portfolio printing + review.

item.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Studio Residency Grant 2026
item.description: 4–6 week fully funded residency for artists at any career stage at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Work independently in one of five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Grant includes $350/week stipend, up to $500 for materials, up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US, free onsite housing, and 24/7 studio access. Applications open February 15; residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $350/week + materials + housing.

item.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Anita Wetzel Residency Grant 2026
item.description: 4–6 week fully funded residency for mature artists aged 45 and older at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Honors the legacy of Anita Lynn Wetzel. Work in any of five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Grant includes $350/week stipend, up to $500 for materials, up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US, free onsite housing, and 24/7 studio access. Residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application. — Deadline: May 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $350/week + materials + housing.

item.title: Shutter Hub Editions Photobook Award 2026
item.description: Photobook award from Shutter Hub Editions celebrating bold storytelling and compelling visual narratives. Particularly welcomes photographers creating their first book. Selected by Karen Harvey MBE, Founder and Creative Director of Shutter Hub. A shortlist of six photographers will be celebrated with a dedicated feature, and selected photographers are invited to contribute a Close Up feature, reaching an audience of over 500,000 people. Winning book published by Shutter Hub Editions with 40% commission on profits paid to the photographer. Submit a written proposal and a PDF with 20+ images. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: £25. Prize: Publication + feature.

item.title: VCCA Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation Fellowship in Photography
item.description: Two-week fully-funded residency at Mt. San Angelo in Amherst, Virginia for US citizens or permanent residents. Supported by the Phillip and Edith Leonian Foundation, established in 2009 to support photographic education and documentary photography. Includes private bedroom with en-suite bath, individual studio space plus darkroom access, and three meals daily in a cross-disciplinary community. Residency dates available May 1 – August 31, 2027. Applications open June 1, 2026. Fee waivers available on request by September 10, 2026. Apply via SlideRoom. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: 2-week funded residency.

item.title: Stories: Narrative Photography · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring narrative and storytelling. Seeking photographs that tell stories — personal or social, literal or symbolic, about persons, communities, objects, or places. All creative photographic interpretations welcome. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD, Rutgers; founder/director PH21 Gallery; Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; Photolucida juror). Curator's choice receives three free entries for future PH21 exhibitions. Up to three honorable mentions. Special rate for students, unwaged, and low-income economies (€15–20). Images submitted by email as JPEG, longest side max 1280px. Early bird deadline May 18 at reduced rates; final deadline May 25. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, July 25 – August 18, 2026. — Deadline: May 25, 2026. Fee: €25–45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PORTAL · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Juried photography exhibition exploring the theme 'at the edge of becoming.' Seeking photographs depicting transition as a condition — figures between visibility and disappearance, spaces suggesting restricted entry, suspended moments, or structurally unstable compositions. The strongest images will resist resolution, embodying transition rather than describing it. Juried by Douglas Stockdale (visual artist, editor, educator; founder of PhotoBook Journal; work in collections at Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma, Beinecke Library at Yale, Reminders Photography Stronghold). All photographic styles and processes accepted. Exhibition June 20 – August 20, 2026. — Deadline: June 3, 2026. Fee: $25/8 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Emergence Project 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Annual graduate showcase for recently graduated UK-based photographers (graduated 2023–2026). Free to submit. Gallery covers all printing and installation costs, with work printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Submit up to 8 images along with a brief statement about your work, graduation details, and why you'd like to participate. Exhibition July 3–31, 2026 at Glasgow Gallery of Photography. — Deadline: May 23, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Across America 2026 · The Art Center
item.description: Photography exhibition celebrating America's diverse and dynamic essence — landscapes, people, culture, or any aspect that embodies the nation's spirit. Up to 3 images forming a cohesive series. Juried by Brian Crowley (landscape/street photographer) and Ron St. Jean (portrait/fine art photographer, 40+ years experience). Exhibition at The Art Center gallery in historic downtown Dover. Artists receive 70% of sale price. All work must be for sale and cannot be removed during the exhibition. Members enter free. Open to US photographers of all levels, 18+. Exhibition July 13 – August 31, 2026. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: $25/3 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Fine Art Photography Awards 2026/2027
item.description: 13th edition of the international fine art photography contest. 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Experimental, Fashion, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Night Photography, Nudes, Open Theme, Panoramic, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Seascape, Street Photography, Travel, Wildlife/Animals. Professional and Amateur divisions. Early bird deadline October 11, 2026; final deadline February 14, 2027. Winners announced April 11, 2027. Panel of 15 international jurors. Professional Grand Prize: $3,000 + Fine Art Photographer of the Year title. Amateur Grand Prize: $2,000. Category winners receive gold/silver/bronze awards. Open worldwide. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $19–34. Prize: $3,000.

item.title: Black and White · Decode Gallery
item.description: Celebrating the power and timelessness of black and white photography — the deep, unending shades of grey. All photographic genres welcome. At least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing and custom matting. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition July 4 – July 25, 2026. — Deadline: May 23, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Global Ability Photography Challenge 2026 · Not Just Art
item.description: 5th edition of the world's largest inclusive photography competition, exclusively for persons with disabilities. Open to all styles — documentary, portrait, street, conceptual, abstract, or experimental. No theme restriction, no age limit. Top 20 photographs exhibited in Ahmedabad, India, with works featured across media and global campaigns. Custom trophies by designer Michael Foley. Award ceremony June 24, 2026. Travel and accommodation support provided for winners. Over 4 editions, GAPC has reached 8 million people and 50,000+ participants from 30+ countries. Organized by Not Just Art (Youth4Jobs) with Adani GreenXTalks. — Deadline: May 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000 total.

item.title: #HopperHappens Juried Photography Exhibition · Edward Hopper House Museum
item.description: Photography-only juried exhibition inspired by the #HopperHappens Instagram series — real-world moments evoking Edward Hopper's style, light, and mood. 55 photographs selected and displayed across 55 businesses and nonprofits in Nyack, NY, birthplace of Edward Hopper. $1,000 in cash prizes: First $500, Second $300, Third $200, plus Juror's and Visitor's Choice awards. Juror: Richard Tuschman, celebrated for his 'Hopper Meditations' series. Exhibition June 1 – July 5, 2026. Open internationally, ages 18+. Work must be completed after January 1, 2020 and never previously exhibited at EHHM. MFA student discounts available. — Deadline: May 3, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $60 non-members. Prize: $500.

item.title: Narrative · Chico Art Center
item.description: Photography exhibition exploring visual storytelling through single images or cohesive series. Documentary, street, conceptual, staged, and experimental approaches welcome. Exhibition at Chico Art Center gallery, August 15 – September 18, 2026, with opening reception September 4. Member fee $25. Free exhibition catalog via Blurb. Opportunity to sell work (30% commission to center). Previously exhibited work at CAC ineligible. — Deadline: June 14, 2026. Fee: $35/7 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Flatland Feature — Issue 2 · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: Online photography feature showcasing photographers' work in a series format as a virtual gallery experience. Selected photographers' work featured for six months on the MWCP website (July–December 2026). Each feature consists of 10–20 images with an accompanying artist statement and biography. Visitors can view and purchase photographs online (50% commission). Open internationally, all subject matter and genres accepted. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: $100/10 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: The Art of Abandonment · TCG Gallery
item.description: International open call exploring abandoned and rediscovered objects, locations, and structures. Photographers examine what these forgotten spaces reveal about humanity, memory, and the passage of time. Online exhibition June 1 – July 1, 2026. Curator's Choice, Director's Choice, and Honorable Mentions awarded. Blind jury process — juror sees only the image and title. — Deadline: May 20, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition + awards.

item.title: Encontros Da Imagem Award 2026 · Encontros da Imagem
item.description: Open call for the 36th edition of Encontros da Imagem, one of Europe's oldest photography festivals, founded in 1991 in Braga, Portugal. Three projects selected for solo exhibitions during the festival across multiple northern Portuguese cities, September 18 – November 1, 2026. One overall winner receives €2,000. Seventeen further projects included in a collective video screening. Theme: Territory And Identity. Projects must use photography or video with coherent narrative structure, produced within the last five years. Maximum three projects per applicant. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: €2,000 + solo exhibition.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — June & July 2026 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome. One artist selected for the combined June/July double issue. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent. — Deadline: April 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: The Paula Riff Award 2026 · Center for Photographic Art
item.description: Annual award honoring artist Paula Riff's legacy, recognizing artists who challenge conventional photography through lensless photography, historical/alternative photographic processes, or physical intervention such as cutting, sewing, and collage. Created in 2021 by the Center for Photographic Art and Lenscratch. $1,000 prize plus featured on Lenscratch and the CPA website. Related group exhibition Changing the Narrative: the First 5 Years of Paula Riff Award Winners opens June 20 at CPA in Carmel. Open internationally to artists working at any career stage. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 + featured on Lenscratch & CPA.

item.title: Eddie Adams Workshop 2026
item.description: One of the most prestigious photojournalism programs in the world. 100 emerging photographers selected annually — evenly split between college students and early-career professionals — for a free 4-day seminar in Jeffersonville, NY. Participants work in teams led by top photographers and editors. Late entry available through May 31 at $55. Applicants must be at least 20 years old and have less than six years of full-time professional experience. Photographers holding staff positions at major publications for more than six years are ineligible. — Deadline: May 24, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Workshop fellowship.

item.title: Marilyn Stafford FotoReportage Award 2026 · FotoDocument
item.description: 10th edition. Annual award for professional female photographers towards the completion of a compelling documentary photo essay addressing important social, environmental, economic, or cultural issues. Supported by Nikon. Winner receives £4,000 to support the project. Special celebration of 10 years of the prize in September at POST, Brighton & Hove's new centre for photography. Open globally to female or female-identifying photographers aged 18+ at any career stage. Must have completed at least one previous documentary photo essay and have already started the submitted project. — Deadline: May 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £4,000.

item.title: JGS Fellowship for Photography 2026 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: Five $8,000 unrestricted cash grants for artists working in traditional and experimental photography, including light-based work, alternative processes, or any form in which photography or photographic techniques are pivotal. Open to New York State photography artists living and working outside of New York City. Notifications in summer 2026. — Deadline: May 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $8,000 (5 awarded).

item.title: Light Work Artist-in-Residence 2027
item.description: One-month creative residency in Syracuse, New York. Selected artists receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished artist apartment, 24-hour access to state-of-the-art facilities, and staff support. Work published in a special edition of Contact Sheet: The Light Work Annual with a commissioned essay. Open to all artists working in photography or image-based media from any country. 12–15 artists selected annually. Notifications by December 2026. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $7,500 stipend.

item.title: Doug Pensinger Photography Fund 2026
item.description: Seven $5,000 grants plus yearlong mentorships from industry professionals for emerging sports photographers. The only nonprofit dedicated to providing career development opportunities to emerging sports photographers. Past grantees range from high school students to recent graduates working as freelancers or interns. Applications close May 1. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 (7 awarded).

item.title: XVIII Festival di Fotografia a Capri — Viaggi e Miraggi · Fondazione Capri
item.description: 18th edition of the annual photography festival at Capri organized by Fondazione Capri. Theme: Viaggi e Miraggi (Journeys and Mirages) — inspired by the 200th anniversary of the rediscovery of the Blue Grotto. Exploring journeys both physical and imagined, where photography becomes a gateway between memory and imagination. Winning project exhibited at Certosa di San Giacomo. Production and installation covered by the foundation. Winners announced July 13. Festival in August 2026, with workshops and educational activities in October 2026. Open to photographers worldwide, professionals and amateurs. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition (production covered).

item.title: FeelsZine Issue 27 — Belonging
item.description: Canadian creative zine celebrating its 10th anniversary with Issue 27 themed around belonging. Accepts photography, illustration, art, collage, and typography alongside poetry, essays, and fiction. Art submissions require artist statements and 300dpi files if accepted. Prioritizes Canadian content but open internationally. Include a short bio noting your country of origin. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Abundance · A Photographer's Place
item.description: Exhibition exploring abundance as both presence and paradox — accumulation and scarcity, fullness and absence, wealth and waste. Seeking photographic responses through documentary, staged, abstract, or experimental approaches. Selections based on thematic relevance, technical quality, originality, and artistic vision. Selected artists may have work printed on Canon ImageProGraf Pro-1100 for an additional fee. Exhibition May 1–30, 2026 with opening reception May 1. — Deadline: April 21, 2026. Fee: $35 for 5 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Lucie Foundation Scholarship Program 2026
item.description: Four cash grants supporting emerging and established photographers. Two tracks: Fine Art and Photojournalism/Documentary, each with Professional ($3,000) and Emerging ($1,000) tiers. Documentary Emerging winner also receives a Sony camera and lens. Winners exhibited together at House of Lucie galleries worldwide including Los Angeles, Athens, Budapest, Ostuni, and Samui. Submit project proposal and 20 images. Early bird pricing available through April. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $15–$25. Prize: $3,000 + exhibition.

item.title: After Dark: Night, Sky, and Shadow · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition of photographs created between dusk and dawn. Night and astrophotography, urban and street scenes, long exposures, light painting, and experimental techniques welcome. Juror: Lance Keimig. Up to 35 images in physical gallery, 40 in online gallery, all in printed catalog. — Deadline: May 4, 2026. Fee: $39. Prize: $300 / $200 / $50.

item.title: Camera Work: Shadow and Light · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Juried group show exploring contemporary interpretations of shadow and light. 26 photographs selected for physical exhibition in Portland, OR; 50 additional for online gallery. All 76 images in purchasable catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for selected works. — Deadline: May 8, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Photobook Open Call · Sonntag Grant
item.description: Open call for a fully-funded photobook from the Sonntag Grant for Photography, in collaboration with Replika Publishing. One FLINTA (female, lesbian, inter, non-binary, trans, agender) artist is selected to produce a photobook with Replika Publishing (350+ copies, 50 to artist). Book launch at Bildband Berlin with travel up to €300 and accommodation covered. Projects should be finished or at an advanced stage. Berlin-based grant launched in 2025. Open globally. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: €10. Prize: Fully-funded photobook + book launch.

item.title: 31st National Competition 2026 · Soho Photo Gallery
item.description: Soho Photo Gallery's 31st annual National Competition. Approximately 60 photographs selected for exhibition at the gallery's spacious W23rd Street location in Chelsea, New York. Cash prizes for first ($400) and second ($200) place. Third place and up to four honorable mentions receive prizes from sponsor Archival Methods. Juror: Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects at Museum of the City of New York. Open to photographers who are residents of the United States. Exhibition July 2026. — Deadline: May 9, 2026. Fee: $55 for 1-5 images. Prize: $400 first place + exhibition.

item.title: BLACK & WHITE · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis celebrating monochrome photography as a deliberate creative choice. Up to 74 images selected for exhibition June 20 – July 11, 2026. Awards include Juror's Choice (free entry to three future calls) and Directors' Choice (free entry to two future calls), plus eight honorable mentions. Members receive 10 images for the price of 5. Free submissions available for artists experiencing financial hardship. Juror: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, fine art photographer, printmaker, and founder of All About Photo. — Deadline: May 3, 2026. item.title: Light Dreams · Light Art Space
item.description: Juried exhibition of alternative and historical process photography at Light Art Space gallery in Silver City, New Mexico. Theme explores light as an internal, psychological, and symbolic presence — where light and dreams intersect through hand-made photographic processes. Accepted media: cyanotype, platinum/palladium, silver gelatin, wet-plate collodion, gum bichromate, and other alternative processes. Digital negatives acceptable but straight digital and AI-derived work ineligible. 3D and experimental work encouraged. Open internationally, ages 18+. Gallery actively invites LGBTQ+, Black, Latinx, Indigenous, and artists of color. Exhibition July 4 – September 6, 2026, with reception July 5. Student rate $20. — Deadline: May 19, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 images. Prize: Exhibition.
